Script.name: statmon
Script.script: --[[ Stat Monitor Sean Stoves, 2026-08-01 Everything Aardwolf tells us about the character, in a panel that reflows. Written against the GMCP protocol rather than ported: Mudlet already parses the char.* messages into a table, so this reads gmcp.char and lays it out. That also means it cannot be wrong about a field name - anything the MUD doesn't send simply isn't drawn, rather than showing a label with a nil beside it. If Aardwolf adds a field to char.stats one day it turns up here with no change needed. Informational only. Nothing here sends a command; it draws what has already arrived. Responsive: the grid picks a column count from the panel width, so the same panel is a tall narrow strip down one side or a wide short bar across the top, and the rows re-flow when you drag it. ]] aardkit = aardkit or {} aardkit.statmon = aardkit.statmon or {} local SM = aardkit.statmon local U = aardkit.util.named("Stats") local DEFAULT = { hp = true, mana = true, moves = true, level = true, tnl = true, str = true, int = true, wis = true, dex = true, con = true, luck = true, hr = true, dr = true, align = true, enemy = true, qp = true, tp = true, gold = true, trains = true, pracs = true, } local function defaults() local t = {} for k, v in pairs(DEFAULT) do t[k] = v end return t end local CFG = U.load("statmon", { show = defaults(), style = "grid" }) local ROW_H, PAD, HDR_H = 16, 4, 15 local MINCOL = 118 -- narrower than this and the numbers collide local COL = { hdr = "#e0af68", label = "#8a93a8", val = "#c8d0dc", good = "#3ad07a", warn = "#e0af68", bad = "#f7768e", row = "#141b2d", line = "#3a4a6b", } --- -- what to show -- -- Ordered, because a stat panel that reorders itself between updates is -- unreadable. Anything the MUD doesn't send is skipped rather than drawn with a -- blank beside it, so this can't claim a field Aardwolf stopped sending. -- -- { subtable, key, long label, short label, max subtable, max key } -- -- The key is the gmcp field name, which is also what 'stats on|off ' -- takes. The default set is the one the old statmon showed - the numbers you -- actually check. Name, race, class, clan, tier, remorts, per-level, bank, -- state and foe% are all here and all off until you ask, because a panel you -- have to hunt through is one you stop reading. -- -- The maxes matter more than they look: a trained stat reads 'str 18/25', and -- without the max you can't tell a capped stat from one worth training. Field -- names checked against what Aardwolf actually sends. --- local GROUPS = { { key = "vitals", title = "Vitals", fields = { { "vitals", "hp", "Health", "Hp", "maxstats", "maxhp" }, { "vitals", "mana", "Mana", "Mn", "maxstats", "maxmana" }, { "vitals", "moves", "Moves", "Mvs", "maxstats", "maxmoves" }, }}, { key = "char", title = "Character", fields = { { "base", "name", "Name", "Name" }, { "status", "level", "Level", "Lvl" }, { "status", "tnl", "To level", "TNL" }, { "base", "race", "Race", "Race" }, { "base", "class", "Class", "Cls" }, { "base", "subclass", "Subclass", "Sub" }, { "base", "clan", "Clan", "Clan" }, { "base", "tier", "Tier", "Tier" }, { "base", "remorts", "Remorts", "Rmt" }, { "base", "perlevel", "Per level","P/L" }, }}, { key = "stats", title = "Stats", fields = { { "stats", "str", "Strength", "Str", "maxstats", "maxstr" }, { "stats", "int", "Intelligence", "Int", "maxstats", "maxint" }, { "stats", "wis", "Wisdom", "Wis", "maxstats", "maxwis" }, { "stats", "dex", "Dexterity", "Dex", "maxstats", "maxdex" }, { "stats", "con", "Constitution", "Con", "maxstats", "maxcon" }, { "stats", "luck", "Luck", "Luk", "maxstats", "maxluck" }, }}, { key = "combat", title = "Combat", fields = { { "stats", "hr", "Hitroll", "HR" }, { "stats", "dr", "Damroll", "DR" }, { "status", "align", "Alignment", "Align" }, { "status", "state", "State", "State" }, { "status", "enemy", "Foe", "Foe" }, { "status", "enemypct", "Foe %", "Foe%" }, }}, { key = "worth", title = "Worth", fields = { { "worth", "qp", "Quest pts", "QP" }, { "worth", "tp", "Trivia", "TP" }, { "worth", "gold", "Gold", "Gold" }, { "worth", "bank", "Bank", "Bank" }, { "worth", "trains", "Trains", "Trn" }, { "worth", "pracs", "Pracs", "Prac" }, }}, } -- Aardwolf sends numbers as strings about half the time local function num(v) return tonumber(tostring(v or "")) end local function get(sub, key) local c = gmcp and gmcp.char local t = c and c[sub] local v = t and t[key] if v == nil or v == "" then return nil end return v end -- 'state' is a code; 3 is the only one worth naming and it means you're playing local STATE = { [1] = "login", [2] = "MOTD", [3] = "playing", [9] = "note" } local function pretty(sub, key, v) if key == "state" then return STATE[num(v)] or tostring(v) end local n = num(v) if n and (key == "gold" or key == "bank" or key == "tnl") then return U.commas(n) end return tostring(v) end -- hp/mana/moves get a colour off how much is left local function vitalcol(cur, max) local c, m = num(cur), num(max) if not (c and m and m > 0) then return COL.val end local pct = c / m if pct >= 0.75 then return COL.good end if pct >= 0.35 then return COL.warn end return COL.bad end --- -- panel --- local cells, heads = {}, {} local panel local function cell(i) if not cells[i] then cells[i] = Geyser.Label:new({ name = "aardkit_sm_c" .. i .. "_" .. (panel and panel.gen or 1), x = 0, y = 0, width = 10, height = ROW_H, }, panel.container) end return cells[i] end local function head(i) if not heads[i] then heads[i] = Geyser.Label:new({ name = "aardkit_sm_h" .. i .. "_" .. (panel and panel.gen or 1), x = 0, y = 0, width = 10, height = HDR_H, }, panel.container) end return heads[i] end panel = aardkit.panel.new({ name = "statmon", title = "Stats", x = "20px", y = "480px", width = 260, height = 260, fontSize = 9, wrap = false, onresize = function() if aardkit.statmon.paint then aardkit.statmon.paint() end end, onbuild = function() cells, heads = {}, {} if aardkit.statmon.paint then aardkit.statmon.paint() end end, }) SM.panel = panel --- -- the MUSHclient layout -- -- What the original looked like, for anyone who reads it faster: -- -- Str : [ 352/200] -- HR : [ 255] -- -- Aligned label, aligned bracket, value right-justified inside it, so the -- numbers form a column you read down. That needs a fixed-width font, which is -- why the panel keeps a console even though the grid style doesn't use one - -- HTML labels can't align two values on a row, and that is the whole point of -- this layout. --- local lastframe local function paint_mush() local c = panel.console if not c then return end -- hide the grid's widgets; they'd sit on top of the console for _, t in ipairs({ cells, heads }) do for _, l in ipairs(t) do pcall(function() l:hide() end) end end pcall(function() c:show() end) local rows, lw, vw = {}, 0, 0 for _, g in ipairs(GROUPS) do for _, f in ipairs(g.fields) do local v = CFG.show[f[2]] and get(f[1], f[2]) or nil if v ~= nil then local maxv = f[5] and get(f[5], f[6]) or nil local text = maxv and (tostring(v) .. "/" .. tostring(maxv)) or pretty(f[1], f[2], v) local col = COL.val if maxv and g.key == "vitals" then col = vitalcol(v, maxv) end rows[#rows + 1] = { label = f[4], text = text, col = col, group = g.key } if #f[4] > lw then lw = #f[4] end if #text > vw then vw = #text end end end end if #rows == 0 then local empty = "<#8a93a8>Nothing from the MUD yet.\n" if empty ~= lastframe then lastframe = empty c:clear(); U.outw(c.name, empty) end return end local buf, n = {}, 0 local group = rows[1].group for _, r in ipairs(rows) do if r.group ~= group then n = n + 1; buf[n] = "\n"; group = r.group end n = n + 1 buf[n] = string.format( "<%s>%-" .. lw .. "s <%s>: <%s>[<%s>%" .. vw .. "s<%s>]\n", COL.label, r.label, COL.line, COL.line, r.col, r.text, COL.line) end local frame = table.concat(buf, "", 1, n) if frame == lastframe then return end lastframe = frame c:clear() U.outw(c.name, frame) end function SM.paint() if CFG.style == "mush" then return paint_mush() end -- the console belongs to the other style; get it out of the way if panel.console then pcall(function() panel.console:hide() end) end lastframe = nil return SM.paint_grid() end function SM.paint_grid() local c = panel.container if not c then return end local w = U.px(c.get_width and c:get_width() or c.width) if w < 60 then w = 260 end local inner = w - PAD * 2 -- As many columns as fit, but capped: past four, extra width just makes more -- narrow columns and the labels stay abbreviated forever. Cap it and the -- columns get wider instead, which is what buys the full words. local cols = math.max(1, math.min(4, math.floor(inner / MINCOL))) local cw = math.floor((inner - (cols - 1) * PAD) / cols) local wide = cw >= 150 -- room for "Constitution" rather than "Con" local h = U.px(c.get_height and c:get_height() or c.height) if h < 40 then h = 260 end local ci, hi, y = 0, 0, PAD local clipped = 0 for _, g in ipairs(GROUPS) do do -- what's switched on AND actually arriving, before drawing a header local rows = {} for _, f in ipairs(g.fields) do local v = CFG.show[f[2]] and get(f[1], f[2]) or nil if v ~= nil then local maxv = f[5] and get(f[5], f[6]) or nil -- vitals shade by how much is left; a stat's max is a -- training ceiling, not a warning, so it stays plain local shade = (g.key == "vitals") and maxv rows[#rows + 1] = { label = wide and f[3] or f[4], value = pretty(f[1], f[2], v), col = shade and vitalcol(v, maxv) or COL.val, max = maxv and pretty(f[5], f[6], maxv) or nil, } end end -- Don't draw past the bottom edge. Labels are children of the -- container but Geyser doesn't clip them, so anything laid out -- below the frame just renders on top of whatever is behind the -- panel - which is how the Worth block ended up floating over the -- output. Count what wouldn't fit and say so instead. local need = HDR_H + math.ceil(#rows / cols) * ROW_H if #rows > 0 and y + need > h - ROW_H then clipped = clipped + #rows rows = {} end if #rows > 0 then hi = hi + 1 local h = head(hi) h:move(PAD, y) h:resize(inner, HDR_H) h:setStyleSheet("background-color: transparent; border: 0px;") h:echo(string.format( "%s" .. " %s", COL.hdr, g.title, COL.line, string.rep("_", math.max(4, math.floor(inner / 7) - #g.title - 1)))) h:show() y = y + HDR_H for i, r in ipairs(rows) do ci = ci + 1 local col = (i - 1) % cols local l = cell(ci) l:move(PAD + col * (cw + PAD), y) l:resize(cw, ROW_H) l:setStyleSheet("background-color: transparent; border: 0px;") l:echo(string.format( "%s " .. "%s" .. "%s", COL.label, r.label, r.col, r.value, COL.label, r.max and ("/" .. r.max) or "")) l:show() if col == cols - 1 or i == #rows then y = y + ROW_H end end y = y + 2 end end end if clipped > 0 then ci = ci + 1 local l = cell(ci) l:move(PAD, math.min(y, h - ROW_H)) l:resize(inner, ROW_H) l:setStyleSheet("background-color: transparent; border: 0px;") l:echo(string.format("%d more - " .. "make the panel taller, or 'stats off <field>'", COL.label, clipped)) l:show() end for i = ci + 1, #cells do cells[i]:hide() end for i = hi + 1, #heads do heads[i]:hide() end end --- -- updates -- -- core/50_gmcp.lua does the coalescing: it listens, ticks once a second, and -- calls back only when one of the subtrees we named actually changed. So a -- fight that fires char.vitals forty times a second draws this once, and an -- idle second draws nothing at all. -- -- Repainting per event was what made the panel shift under you mid-combat. --- aardkit.gmcp.watch("statmon", { "char.vitals", "char.maxstats", "char.status", "char.base", "char.stats", "char.worth" }, function() if panel:visible() then SM.paint() end end) --- -- commands --- local function known(key) for _, g in ipairs(GROUPS) do for _, f in ipairs(g.fields) do if f[2] == key then return f, g end end end end function SM.cmd(arg) local verb, rest = U.split_verb(arg) -- 'x opacity 200' where somebody looks for it, rather than only -- 'panel x opacity 200'. One line; core does the work. if aardkit.panel.verb("statmon", verb, rest) then return end rest = U.trim(rest):lower() if verb == "toggle" then SM.paint() panel:toggle() elseif verb == "show" or verb == "hide" or verb == "dock" or verb == "embed" then aardkit.panel.cmd("statmon " .. verb) elseif verb == "on" or verb == "off" then local f = known(rest) if not f then U.warn("No field '" .. rest .. "'. 'stats fields' lists them.") else CFG.show[rest] = (verb == "on") or nil U.save("statmon", CFG) SM.paint() U.ok("Stats: " .. f[3] .. " " .. verb .. ".") end elseif verb == "mush" or verb == "grid" or verb == "style" then if verb ~= "style" then CFG.style = verb U.save("statmon", CFG) lastframe = nil -- the two styles use different widgets, so clear the other's for _, t in ipairs({ cells, heads }) do for _, l in ipairs(t) do pcall(function() l:hide() end) end end SM.paint() panel:show() end U.ok("Stats: " .. (CFG.style == "mush" and "MUSHclient layout - aligned single column, 'stats grid' for the other." or "grid layout - grouped and reflowing, 'stats mush' for the old one.")) elseif verb == "reset" then CFG.show = defaults() U.save("statmon", CFG) SM.paint() U.ok("Stats: back to the default fields.") elseif verb == "fields" then local rows = {} for _, g in ipairs(GROUPS) do rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } rows[#rows + 1] = { g.title } for _, f in ipairs(g.fields) do local live = get(f[1], f[2]) ~= nil rows[#rows + 1] = { " " .. f[2], (CFG.show[f[2]] and "on " or "off") .. " " .. f[3] .. (live and "" or " (not being sent)") } end end rows[#rows + 1] = { "" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "stats on|off ", "add or drop one" } rows[#rows + 1] = { "stats reset", "back to the default set" } U.help("Stat Monitor fields", rows) else U.help("Stat Monitor", { { "stats toggle", "show or hide the panel" }, { "stats", "toggle the panel" }, { "stats fields", "every field, what's on, what the MUD is sending" }, { "stats on|off ", "add one of the extras, or drop one you never read" }, { "stats reset", "back to the default set" }, { "stats mush | grid", "the old aligned column, or the grouped grid" }, { "stats dock|embed|show|hide", "panel placement" }, { "stats opacity <0-255>", "how solid this window is; 'default' follows the shared setting" }, { "" }, { "Read-only. It draws what GMCP has already sent." }, }) end end aardkit.register("stats", "character stats from GMCP, in a panel that reflows", SM.cmd) tempTimer(1, function() SM.paint() end)
